summary: The candidate only replaces the original NoneType crashes with an explicit RuntimeError. It does not make NVFP4 speculative verification work with graphs disabled or enabled, so it is diagnostic hardening rather than an original-issue fix.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before reproduction of all three missing-metadata dereferences, including the issue's extend_prefix_lens_cpu NoneType subscript. Raw log: /job/review-evidence-j-1fabdba9da01/base-regression.log

The candidate converts missing metadata into RuntimeError and preserves the empty-list boundary; 2 tests and 3 subtests passed. It did not measure successful speculative decoding or FP4 attention. Raw log: /job/review-evidence-j-1fabdba9da01/candidate-regression.log
Confirmed the imported Python implementation came from the active checkout at /job/repo/python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/memory_pool.py.

gpu_execution.evidence: A gfx950 AMD Instinct MI355X was visible through ROCm 7.2, but the original contract requires NVIDIA SM120 CUDA FlashInfer/TRTLLM NVFP4. No unrelated AMD smoke is counted as issue execution.

remaining_counterexamples: With CUDA graphs disabled, the first speculative target-verify request still raises and terminates instead of serving successfully; only the exception type/message changes.
With CUDA graphs enabled, request-dependent FP4 workspace page selection is still host-driven inside the captured region and remains unsupported/unsafe.
The test never constructs the GPU-only ForwardBatch used by speculative verification and never demonstrates successful FP4 dequantization or attention output.
The external draft-model backend constraint described by the issue is unchanged.
remaining_limitations: No RTX 5090/SM120 device, CUDA runtime, reported model weights, or NVIDIA NVFP4 FlashInfer/TRTLLM execution path was available.
The candidate changed only Python source and tests; no native rebuild was applicable.
The review establishes control-flow behavior and exception translation, not full-model numerical correctness or performance.
